whatIsFtwz.title: What is an FTWZ & Our 3PL Services
whatIsFtwz.description: A Free Trade Warehousing Zone (FTWZ) is a special category of SEZ (governed under the SEZ Act, 2005) that sits within India's geographic borders but outside its customs territory, enabling:
features: Duty-free storage of imported goods until clearance or re-export
Foreign-currency transactions without needing a local establishment
Value-added operations (labelling, kitting, sampling, etc.) without separate approvals

overview.name: Naphtha
overview.description: A volatile, clear, colorless to pale yellow liquid hydrocarbon mixture used as a petrochemical feedstock, solvent, fuel, and in chemical synthesis.
overview.overviewDescription: Naphtha represents one of the most versatile and crucial intermediate products in the global petrochemical industry. Derived from crude oil refining processes, this light hydrocarbon mixture serves as the backbone for countless industrial applications, from basic fuel components to sophisticated chemical synthesis. Its unique composition of C5-C12 hydrocarbons makes it an indispensable raw material for producing essential chemicals that power modern life, including plastics, synthetic fibers, and specialty solvents.
keyFeatures: Essential petrochemical feedstock for ethylene and propylene production
Versatile solvent for industrial applications including paints, varnishes, and rubber manufacturing
Available in light and heavy grades with different boiling ranges and applications
Critical component in gasoline blending and fuel formulations
Widely used in chemical synthesis for producing aromatic compounds (BTX)
majorApplications: Steam cracking for olefin production
Catalytic reforming for gasoline production
Solvent applications in various industries
Chemical synthesis and manufacturing
overview.industrialSignificance: Naphtha serves as one of the most important building blocks in the petrochemical industry, with global demand driven by growing plastic and polymer production. Its versatility makes it indispensable for both fuel and chemical applications.

identification.commonNames: Light naphtha, Heavy naphtha, Petroleum ether, Ligroin
identification.casNumber: 8030-30-6 (general); other variants may have specific CAS numbers
identification.chemicalFormula: Mixture of C₅–C₁₂ hydrocarbons (mainly alkanes, cycloalkanes, aromatics)

physicalChemicalProperties.odor: Gasoline-like, sweetish (light naphtha) to strong (heavy naphtha)
physicalChemicalProperties.flashPoint: –20 to 60°C (varies; light naphtha is highly flammable)
physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Insoluble in water; miscible with most organic solvents (benzene, ether, chloroform)

gradesPurity.purityNotes: Varies by refining, may contain sulfur, olefins, additives

applications.title: Petrochemical Feedstock
applications.description: Cracked to produce ethylene and propylene (steam cracking); reformed to make gasoline (catalytic reforming).

applications.title: Solvent
applications.description: Used in dry cleaning, paints, varnishes, rubber, and adhesive manufacturing.

applications.title: Fuel
applications.description: Component of gasoline; camping stove fuel (light naphtha).

applications.title: Chemical Synthesis
applications.description: Feedstock for aromatics (BTX: benzene, toluene, xylene).

storageHandling.storage: Airtight containers (prevent evaporation/flammability). Explosion-proof storage (light naphtha). Grounded tanks (static prevention)
storageHandling.handling: Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile, neoprene). Vapor respirators if needed. No open flames/sparks.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Highly flammable (light naphtha flash point < –20°C). Harmful if inhaled (CNS depression). Skin irritant (defats skin). Environmental risk (toxic to aquatic life).
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Flame, Health Hazard. UN 1255 (Petroleum Naphtha), UN 3295 (Hydrocarbon Mixture)

overview.name: Propylene (Propene)
overview.description: A colorless, mildly sweet-smelling gas used primarily for polypropylene production, as a chemical intermediate, fuel gas, and in synthetic rubber manufacturing.
overview.overviewDescription: Propylene emerges as the second most critical olefin in the global petrochemical landscape, driving innovation across packaging, automotive, textiles, and countless other industries. This three-carbon alkene molecule serves as the gateway to an extensive family of polymers and chemicals that define modern manufacturing. From the ubiquitous polypropylene plastics found in everything from food containers to automotive components, to specialized chemical intermediates that enable advanced materials production, propylene's versatility and economic importance continue to grow with expanding global demand.
keyFeatures: Second most important olefin after ethylene in petrochemical industry
Primary raw material for polypropylene plastic production (65% of global demand)
Available in multiple grades: polymer, chemical, and refinery grade
Key building block for numerous chemical intermediates and derivatives
Essential component in LPG blends and fuel applications
majorApplications: Polypropylene production for packaging and automotive applications
Acrylonitrile manufacturing for acrylic fibers
Propylene oxide production for polyurethanes
Cumene synthesis for phenol and acetone production
overview.industrialSignificance: Propylene is the second most important building block in the petrochemical industry after ethylene, with global demand exceeding 100 million tons annually. Its versatility in producing both commodity and specialty chemicals makes it crucial for modern manufacturing.

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Slightly soluble in water, soluble in organic solvents

applications.title: Chemical Intermediate
applications.description: For acrylonitrile (acrylic fibers), propylene oxide (polyurethanes), cumene (phenol/acetone).

storageHandling.storage: Pressurized steel cylinders (small quantities), refrigerated tanks (large volumes, -48°C), grounded containers (static prevention)
storageHandling.handling: Use explosion-proof equipment, continuous gas detection, SCBA for leaks

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Extremely flammable (LFL 2.0%, UFL 11.1%). Asphyxiant (displaces oxygen). Frostbite risk from liquefied gas contact.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Flame, Gas Cylinder. Transport Class: UN 1077 (Class 2.1 Flammable Gas).

overview.name: Benzene
overview.description: A colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet odor, serving as a fundamental building block in petrochemical industry.
overview.overviewDescription: Benzene stands as the cornerstone of aromatic chemistry and one of the most fundamental building blocks in the modern chemical industry. This simple yet powerful six-carbon ring molecule has revolutionized manufacturing across multiple sectors, from plastics and synthetic materials to pharmaceuticals and specialty chemicals. Its unique aromatic structure provides exceptional stability and reactivity, making it the starting point for an enormous variety of downstream products that are essential to contemporary industrial processes and consumer goods.
keyFeatures: Fundamental aromatic hydrocarbon and building block for numerous chemicals
High-purity grades available for pharmaceutical and specialty applications
Essential precursor for styrene, phenol, and cyclohexane production
Critical component in synthetic rubber and plastic manufacturing
Widely used in chemical synthesis and as an industrial solvent
majorApplications: Styrene production for polystyrene plastics
Phenol manufacturing via cumene process
Cyclohexane production for nylon manufacturing
Chemical intermediate and solvent applications
overview.industrialSignificance: Benzene is one of the most important basic chemicals in the petrochemical industry, with global production exceeding 50 million tons annually. Its aromatic structure makes it indispensable for producing a wide range of downstream chemicals and materials.

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Slightly soluble in water, miscible with organic solvents

applications.title: Styrene Production
applications.description: Major feedstock for producing styrene monomer used in polystyrene

applications.title: Phenol Manufacturing
applications.description: Key raw material for phenol production via cumene process

applications.title: Cyclohexane Production
applications.description: Used to produce cyclohexane for nylon manufacturing

applications.title: Chemical Solvents
applications.description: Industrial solvent for various chemical processes

storageHandling.storage: Store in tightly closed containers in a cool, well-ventilated area away from ignition sources.
storageHandling.handling: Use chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and work in a fume hood. Avoid inhalation and skin contact.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Highly flammable. Toxic by inhalation, skin absorption, and ingestion. Carcinogenic. Environmental hazard.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS: Flame, Health Hazard. UN 1114 (Class 3, Flammable Liquid). OSHA PEL: 1 ppm (8-hour TWA). IARC Group 1 (carcinogenic to humans).

overview.name: Red Phosphorus
overview.description: An amorphous, odorless, brittle, non-crystalline allotrope of phosphorus, widely used in flame retardants, matches, pyrotechnics, semiconductors, and chemical synthesis.
overview.overviewDescription: Red phosphorus represents a safer and more stable alternative to its highly toxic white phosphorus counterpart, playing crucial roles across multiple high-tech and traditional industries. This amorphous allotrope has become indispensable in modern electronics manufacturing, fire safety applications, and specialized chemical processes. Its unique properties—combining chemical reactivity with relative safety—make it an essential component in everything from semiconductor doping to advanced flame retardant systems that protect lives and property.
keyFeatures: Safer alternative to white phosphorus with reduced toxicity
Essential component in flame retardant formulations for electronics and textiles
Critical dopant material in semiconductor manufacturing
Key ingredient in safety match striking surfaces
